You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From fea3fdf975dd9f3e5248afaab8fe023db313f005 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jiasheng Jiang <jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2021 09:41:26 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] drm/ast: potential dereference of null pointer

The return value of kzalloc() needs to be checked.
To avoid use of null pointer '&ast_state->base' in case of the
failure of alloc.

Fixes: f0adbc382b8b ("drm/ast: Allocate initial CRTC state of the correct size")
Signed-off-by: Jiasheng Jiang <jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20211214014126.2211535-1-jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn
---
 drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c | 5 ++++-
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c
index 1e30eaeb0e1b..d5c98f79d58d 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c
@@ -1121,7 +1121,10 @@ static void ast_crtc_reset(struct drm_crtc *crtc)
 	if (crtc->state)
 		crtc->funcs->atomic_destroy_state(crtc, crtc->state);
 
-	__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, &ast_state->base);
+	if (ast_state)
+		__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, &ast_state->base);
+	else
+		__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, NULL);
 }
 
 static struct drm_crtc_state *
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a potential dereference of a null pointer when the `kzalloc()` function failed to allocate memory for `ast_state`. The code did not check if `ast_state` was successfully allocated before using it, which could lead to dereferencing a null pointer and causing a crash or undefined behavior. The patch adds a check to ensure that `ast_state` is not null before using it in the `__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset` function.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a potential dereference of a null pointer when the `kzalloc()` function failed to allocate memory for `ast_state`. The code did not check if `ast_state` was successfully allocated before using it, which could lead to dereferencing a null pointer and causing a crash or undefined behavior. The patch adds a check to ensure that `ast_state` is not null before using it in the `__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset` function.
